body.statement: On the full real cube \(p\in[0,1]^{E^{?}}\), \(R_{XY}(p)=\sum_{S\subseteq E^{?}:\operatorname{Fail}(S)=0}\prod_{e\in S}p_e\prod_{e\in E^{?}\setminus S}(1-p_e)\) is a multilinear polynomial and \(\partial R_{XY}/\partial p_e=-\Pr_{p_{-e}}\{\operatorname{Fail}(Z\setminus\{e\})=0,\operatorname{Fail}(Z\cup\{e\})=1\}\in[-1,0]\), including at boundary points by polynomial evaluation. On the interior cube \(p\in(0,1)^{E^{?}}\), the same polynomial satisfies \(R_{XY}(p)=\prod_{e\in E^{?}}(1-p_e)\,I_{\mathcal O}((p_e/(1-p_e))_{e\in E^{?}})\).
body.justification: This is an algebraic implementation corollary of compiling the monotone failure event into its minimal-support antichain, not an independent novelty claim.
body.gap: Akbari et al. use products of edge probabilities to rank one realization; after the new obstruction compiler makes the negative monotone clauses explicit, the total mass and pivotal-edge derivative identities follow by standard literal weighting and conditioning.
body.consumer: Practitioners obtain total confidence and the marginal value of resolving uncertainty about each edge from the compiler output.
